resources.string: Uterine lining area: a cylinder analogy
Model side area (LU²) = 2π × inner radius (LU) × length (LU). At a fixed length, a larger radius gives more area. At a fixed radius, a longer cylinder gives more area.

Endometrial epithelial cells cover the inner surface of the uterine body as part of the endometrium. The cervical canal has its own mucus-secreting columnar lining, not endometrium. Both have an inner surface, like a lining inside an open tube. This model counts only the curved inner wall of a smooth cylinder, not either end. Its dimensions use invented length units (LU) and do not represent the shape or size of either anatomical space.
